```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

root_candidates <- normalizePath(c(".", "..", "../.."), mustWork = FALSE)
repo_root <- root_candidates[file.exists(file.path(root_candidates, "support_files", "qc_helpers.R"))][[1L]]
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo_root)
```

This report runs the fast, local `testthat` checks. It does not submit SLURM
jobs or require real CellRanger matrices. Matrix-reading tests create small
filtered/raw 10x MEX fixtures in temporary directories.

## Environment

Run from the repository's R environment. In a shell, initialize it before
rendering:

```bash
unset R_HOME R_LIBS R_LIBS_USER R_PROFILE R_PROFILE_USER R_ENVIRON R_ENVIRON_USER
set +u
source /gpfs/data/cvrcbioinfolab/gildem01/conda_envs/anaconda3/condaload_r.sh
set -u
Rscript --vanilla -e 'rmarkdown::render("tests/testing.Rmd")'
```

The test suite needs `testthat` and `Matrix`; the synthetic 10x reader test
also uses `Seurat`. The report uses `knitr` and `rmarkdown`.

```{r package-status}
required_packages <- c("testthat", "Matrix", "Seurat", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
package_status <- data.frame(
  package = required_packages,
  installed = vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(package_status, row.names = FALSE)

if (!all(package_status$installed[package_status$package %in% c("testthat", "Matrix", "knitr", "rmarkdown")])) {
  stop("Install the required testing/report packages before running this report.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

## Local Tests

The suite checks:

- HTO/ADT feature splitting by the canonical `feature_reference.csv` `name`
  values, including strict errors for missing names.
- Transposed sample-sheet loading, header validation, missing/duplicate
  fields, and sample selection.
- ADT count MAD defaults, explicit min/max thresholds, filter boundaries, and
  no-op behavior when ADT is disabled.
- Actual `Seurat::Read10X()` parsing of generated filtered/raw MEX fixtures.
- R/R Markdown parsing, the fixed HTO quantile, Singlet-only mask and
  Singlet-derived HTO plot thresholds, shell syntax, and sample-name
  extraction from the transposed CSV header.

```{r run-testthat, results='asis'}
rscript <- Sys.which("Rscript")
if (!nzchar(rscript)) stop("Rscript is not available on PATH.", call. = FALSE)

test_run <- local({
  previous_dir <- getwd()
  on.exit(setwd(previous_dir))
  setwd(repo_root)
  output <- system2(rscript, c("--vanilla", "tests/testthat.R"),
                    stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  status <- attr(output, "status")
  list(output = output, status = if (is.null(status)) 0L else status)
})
cat(test_run$output, sep = "\n")
if (test_run$status != 0L) stop("The local testthat suite failed.", call. = FALSE)
```

The same suite can run without rendering this report:

```bash
Rscript --vanilla tests/testthat.R
```

## Cluster Smoke Checks

The local suite does not render the full QC workflow. After replacing the
`Pool_1` placeholder matrix, feature-reference, and raw ADT paths in
`samples.csv`, perform these checks in the cluster R environment:

1. Render one RNA-only sample and compare its QC output with the existing
   RNA-only workflow.
2. Render one hashtagged+CITE-seq sample. Confirm HTO Singlets are retained,
   the `ADT_DSB` assay is created, and the ADT count filter is reported.
3. For a mixed run, confirm merged sample/library metadata and the HTO/ADT
   report sections.
4. Check `chunk_logs/chunk_progress_<sample>.log` for the ADT threshold
   parameters.

Before the HTO/ADT render, confirm `dsb`, `scater`, and `gridExtra`
are installed. These full-data checks require usable CellRanger matrices and
are intentionally kept out of the fast local suite.
